L12-2b06c9: **Bladder neck contracture (BNC)** is pathologic narrowing of the native bladder neck that causes bladder outlet obstruction. On WARWIKI, this page uses BNC primarily for the post-benign-outlet-procedure entity: scarring after TURP, bipolar TURP, HoLEP / endoscopic enucleation, laser vaporization, bladder-neck incision, or radiation-treated outlet tissue. Narrowing at the post-radical-prostatectomy vesicourethral anastomosis is handled separately as [vesicourethral anastomotic stenosis](/docs/clinical-conditions/03b-voiding-outlet/vesicourethral-anastomotic-stenosis) (VUAS).
L14-0675fd: The distinction is practical. In BNC, the prostate or prostatic fossa may still be present and the external sphincter is usually distal and intact. In VUAS, the prostate is absent and the scar sits immediately proximal to the membranous urethra, so every incision or reconstruction carries a higher continence penalty.
L35-c707c0: BNC incidence depends on the index outlet procedure, definition, and follow-up. Contemporary series after transurethral prostate surgery report BNC in roughly 1-6% of patients (2% overall in one 1,008-patient series, 6.4% needing further surgery after TURP in another), with higher rates after bipolar TURP than enucleation in some cohorts.<sup>[[1]](#ref1)[[2]](#ref2)[[4]](#ref4)</sup> A meta-analysis of 28 RCTs found no significant difference in BNC between enucleation and TURP, so a lower enucleation rate should not be assumed.<sup>[[14]](#ref14)</sup>
L52-93d50f: BNC is a circumferential scar response at the bladder neck. The reconstructive mechanism is familiar: ischemic mucosa, failed epithelial apposition, inflammation, urinary extravasation, infection, and repeated trauma heal by contraction rather than a stable epithelialized lumen.
L56-9942e9: - **Small gland or small resection cavity:** less tissue removed, less funneling, and a tighter healing ring after TURP
L57-8573c2: - **Thermal injury:** coagulation at the bladder neck creates deeper ischemic fibrosis
L58-8d434b: - **Positive urine culture / UTI:** inflammation during healing increases scar burden
L59-ba63e1: - **Repeat instrumentation:** catheter trauma, secondary transurethral intervention, and early reoperation add injury
L60-5eef87: - **Microvascular disease:** smoking, diabetes, hypertension, coronary disease, and radiation reduce tissue reserve
L61-bbc99e: - **Under-treated outlet obstruction:** persistent high-pressure voiding can worsen symptoms even with a moderate scar
L75-3c0be2: In TURP cohorts, smaller prostate volume, positive urine culture or preoperative UTI, and secondary transurethral intervention repeatedly emerge as practical warning signs.<sup>[[1]](#ref1)[[2]](#ref2)[[3]](#ref3)[[4]](#ref4)</sup>
L99-07788a: - **Urinalysis and culture:** treat infection before incision

L101-7857a0: - **Cystoscopy:** diagnostic test; defines lumen caliber, tissue quality, proximity to sphincter, stones, false passages, and catheterizability
L102-4b490b: - **RUG / VCUG:** useful when posterior urethral stricture, VUAS, or complex anatomy is possible
L103-0f9f85: - **Urodynamics:** selected cases with underactive bladder, severe urgency, neurogenic concern, or discordant symptoms
L109-ce8655: If the patient has had radical prostatectomy, radical cystectomy with orthotopic neobladder, or a prostate-absent outlet, use the [VUAS framework](/docs/clinical-conditions/03b-voiding-outlet/vesicourethral-anastomotic-stenosis). A bladder neck contracture label after prostatectomy often hides a different continence and reconstruction problem.

L164-76a4eb: TUITMR adapts a Y-V-plasty concept endoscopically: scar is incised and healthy bladder mucosa is advanced transversely across the defect with endoscopic suturing. In 19 patients (47% BNC, 53% VUAS; median follow-up 6 months), patency was 89% after one procedure and 100% after two, without de novo incontinence; comparative and long-term data are lacking.<sup>[[8]](#ref8)</sup>
L166-c14362: Robotic reconstruction is the usual next step after repeated endoscopic failure in a fit patient.
